title: Workspace And Server Read Surfaces
objective: Prove the server-owned registry and first product-facing read slices by moving status, capabilities, and workspace inventory onto Server V2.

steps.name: Define the server registry service surface
steps.description: Create typed services for reading local and remote server targets from the DB so route handlers and app adapters can share one source of truth.
successFactors: Server target lookup is reusable and testable.
The service exposes enough metadata for routing and capability checks.
No feature code needs raw DB access to inspect server targets.

steps.name: Define the workspace registry service surface
steps.description: Create typed services for listing, filtering, resolving, and serializing workspaces so the API and app can move onto the canonical server-owned registry model.
successFactors: Workspace resolution is centralized.
The service can return hidden and visible workspaces intentionally.
The code clearly separates local, remote, control, and help workspace handling.

steps.name: Implement the capabilities model
steps.description: Add the Server V2 capabilities summary, including at least the V2 capability signal and relevant runtime/auth flags, so clients can detect what the server can do.
successFactors: Capabilities come from server-owned logic rather than hardcoded UI assumptions.
The model can grow as new slices land.
The response is available through a typed route and reusable service.

steps.name: Implement normalized system status routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 status or summary routes that expose health, uptime, registry summary, and capabilities in the new API shape rather than legacy payloads.
successFactors: Status payloads come from the new server and match the desired namespace.
The route is usable by app startup and settings surfaces.
Legacy-only fields are either mapped intentionally or omitted deliberately.

steps.name: Implement `GET /workspaces`
steps.description: Expose the primary workspace inventory route that returns visible workspaces from the server-owned registry in a stable shape.
successFactors: The route returns workspace records from the DB and service layer.
Normal user-facing listing excludes hidden control/help workspaces by default.
The route is fully typed and documented.

steps.name: Implement workspace detail routes
steps.description: Add routes for reading a single workspace and its summary metadata so the UI can fetch detail views without reconstructing workspace information locally.
successFactors: Workspace detail responses are stable and typed.
The route handles local and remote workspaces cleanly.
Errors for missing or inaccessible workspaces use the shared error model.

steps.name: Implement hidden workspace filtering rules
steps.description: Make hidden control/help workspaces explicit in the registry and route behavior so later internal surfaces can use them without polluting normal workspace lists.
successFactors: Hidden workspace behavior is intentional, not ad hoc filtering.
Admin or internal readers can still fetch hidden workspaces when needed.
The listing behavior is covered by tests.

steps.name: Implement workspace backend resolution
steps.description: Add the service that resolves whether a workspace is backed by local OpenCode or a remote OpenWork server so later read and write slices can route consistently.
successFactors: Each workspace resolves to exactly one backend type.
Routing data is derived from canonical registry state.
The resolution service can be reused by session and file phases.

steps.name: Define local workspace serialization
steps.description: Decide and implement the public summary fields for local workspaces, including status, display metadata, config/data paths where appropriate, and backend identifiers that should stay server-private.
successFactors: Public responses expose OpenWork IDs instead of leaking OpenCode IDs unnecessarily.
The serialization shape is consistent across list and detail routes.
Sensitive internal fields remain server-owned.

steps.name: Define remote workspace serialization
steps.description: Decide and implement the public summary fields for remote workspaces so the app can render them through one workspace-first model without handling remote server details itself.
successFactors: Remote workspaces fit the same public model as local workspaces where practical.
Remote backend IDs are kept behind the server boundary.
The route shape supports later remote session routing work.

steps.name: Add optional server inventory reads if needed
steps.description: Expose any needed server-target read routes or internal query surfaces required for settings, remote-connect flows, or debugging, without making server identity more user-facing than necessary.
successFactors: The UI can inspect needed server target metadata through the main server.
Server inventory remains a system concern rather than a UI-side reconstructed graph.
The route surface stays minimal and intentional.

steps.name: Add auth and scope checks for read surfaces
steps.description: Implement the minimum auth and visibility rules required for system status, workspace list, and workspace detail endpoints so early read slices do not ship without a security model.
successFactors: Read routes honor the chosen auth boundary.
Unauthorized clients receive consistent typed failures.
The rules are simple enough to extend later without breaking payloads.

steps.name: Migrate app startup workspace discovery
steps.description: Move the app's initial workspace discovery path to Server V2 through the new adapter so the UI stops reconstructing registry state locally when the flag is on.
successFactors: Workspace bootstrap uses the new adapter and read routes.
Legacy fallback remains available while rollout is incomplete.
The UI can render the first real server-backed workspace list.

steps.name: Migrate workspace switcher and sidebar summaries
steps.description: Point the first visible workspace list and summary UI surfaces at the new Server V2 read routes so the migration has a user-facing proof point.
successFactors: At least one production-like visible workspace surface is fully backed by Server V2.
The UI does not need local registry rebuild logic for the migrated surface.
Any payload differences are normalized at the boundary.

steps.name: Normalize legacy and V2 workspace payloads
steps.description: Ensure the adapter returns one stable workspace summary/detail shape to the UI while some code paths still use legacy responses.
successFactors: The rest of the UI does not fork on payload shape.
Normalization stays near the transport boundary.
The normalized model is documented in code or tests.

steps.name: Add registry and workspace read tests
steps.description: Write tests for local-only, mixed local/remote, and hidden-workspace cases so the server-owned registry model is verified before write-heavy phases depend on it.
successFactors: The main workspace read routes are covered by automated tests.
Hidden workspaces and backend resolution are asserted explicitly.
The tests prove the registry is server-owned and stable.

steps.name: Add app integration coverage for migrated reads
steps.description: Add tests or reliable verification for app boot, workspace discovery, and switcher behavior in Server V2 mode so the first migrated UI slice is guarded against regression.
successFactors: The migrated UI surfaces are exercised with the rollout flag on.
Legacy mode still remains available as a comparison path.
Developers can tell if the first proof slice regresses.

steps.name: Capture remaining registry open questions
steps.description: If there is still uncertainty around public workspace shape, hidden workspace behavior, or server inventory exposure, log it in `open-questions.md` and continue with the best guess.
successFactors: Registry assumptions are visible to later phases.
Any best-guess payload choices are recorded.
Phase 5 leaves later session and file phases with a stable workspace resolution model.
